title: Hold a sock still on a clothesline in a breeze with one hand while the other clips a clothespin over it
instruction: Hold the sock still on the line with one hand; with the other take the clothespin by its handle, squeeze it open, bring it down astride the line over the sock and let go so it clips on; then let go of the sock.
context: Hanging out washing is a two-handed household chore: in a breeze the sock keeps swinging about the line, so one hand holds it still against the line while the other squeezes a clothespin open and clips it on. A clothespin snapped at a sock that is swinging about catches only air or a corner of it.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed clothesline: a stainless-steel rod 6 mm thick, 6 cm above the table and 30 cm forward, running across the table between two wooden posts 17.5 cm right and 17.5 cm left of the centre line. (2) A loose green cotton sock, 20 g, 22 cm long, folded over the line along its length, from 12 cm right of the centre line to 10 cm left of it: a fold on the line and two stiff sides 5 cm deep hanging down either side. A breeze pushes it to and fro across the line (up to 0.05 N, every 1.2 s), swinging it up to about 55 degrees either way unless it is held. (3) A loose wooden clothespin, 8 g, standing upright in a plastic holder 22 cm forward and 16 cm right of the centre line: two jaws 5 cm long, 12 mm wide and 5 mm thick, joined at the top by a steel spring hinge (the fulcrum), and a handle block 14 x 12 x 35 mm above the fulcrum on the fixed jaw (the one on the side nearer the arm bases). Squeezing the handle (a gripper's fingers closed on it) swings the other jaw open to 35 degrees; letting go, the spring shuts it. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. On the line: the line runs between the pin's jaws (within 12 mm across from the fulcrum, from 4 mm below it to 3 mm above the jaws' tips), the pin within 30 degrees of upright. Over the sock: the pin along the sock, at least 6 mm in from either end, and the sock on the line. Hung: the sock's fold within 1 cm of its place on the line and its sides within 20 degrees of hanging straight down. Clipped: the pin let go (its handle released) on the line over the sock while the other gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) was holding the sock (within 3 cm of it across, from its lower edge up to 3 cm above its fold, and no more than 1 cm past either end); let go over a sock that nobody holds, it does not catch. 1.0: clipped, on the line over the sock, the sock hung, and both TCPs clear (at least 6 cm from the pin's fulcrum and 4 cm from the sock); 0.5: clipped, but a hand still on the pin or the sock, or the sock not hung; 0.25: the pin on the line without being clipped; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the sock and the pin still.
reset_notes: Hang the sock back over the line where it was and stand the clothespin, shut, in its holder.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the sock is one rigid body (a fold and two stiff sides) that swings about the line; the breeze is a sideways force on it. While fingers are closed on the pin's handle, the jaw is driven open; let go, a spring shuts it. A pin let go over the sock while the other hand holds it is fixed there with the sock; over an unheld sock it is not. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
